reading.body:
The Weaver is an OpenStreetMap record tagged as a data center that gives no positive evidence of being one. Its name points to textiles, craft, or a hospitality business, not to IT or hosting.

The record carries no megawatts, no operator, no website, and no confirmed business identity. It sits in Spain, 1.9 miles from Alicante-Elche Miguel Hernández Airport, a location that fits a warehouse or commercial premises as easily as a compute facility. The tag itself is the only thing asserting a data center exists here.

For AI infrastructure, this matters as a caution about the source layer. Facility counts built from volunteered geographic data inherit the errors of that data, and a single mistagged node can inflate a regional total. The absence of a power figure is the sharper gap, because compute capacity is ultimately bounded by delivered electricity, and this record says nothing about it.

What the data does not establish is whether The Weaver is a data center at all. The research status is exhausted, meaning the mistag hypothesis was neither confirmed nor ruled out. Nothing here should be read as evidence of capacity, operator, or grid load in Spain.
